content.rendered:
This one’s for the completists (like me).

For all the many songs Bruce has recorded or performed over the years, there are so many more that never saw the light of day.

Some of them have surfaced in old, yellowing notebooks over the years, often through on-line auctions that provide fans  with a peek into Bruce’s early songwriting process. The most notable of these are the ones Bruce transcribed in his “1968 Notebook,” many of which I’ve blogged about here (and the rest of which are topics for later essays). Those early, pre-label compositions feature mostly or fully fleshed-out lyrics, and some even have chord notations.

But here’s one that Bruce seems to have abandoned almost as soon as he started. With nothing to go one–no title, no chords, no date, barely even a verse–it’s a curiosity at best. I wouldn’t even know if its existence had this photograph not found its way to Brucebase.

Bruce seems to be teeing up some kind of environmental message, but that’s pure speculation, since we have nothing else to go by.

In Kansas, a dust storm was raging
In West Virginia, the dam was breaking
In Arizona, a million dollars in desert was being blown into the sky
And in heaven, clouds were shifting

And while the composition is undated, I would peg it circa 1971-1972, based purely on the paper itself–the rounded corners, three-hole punch, and unperforated pages match closely snapshots of the notebook(s) Bruce wrote in during that time. (If you have any additional background on this composition, I’d love to know it.)

In Kansas
Never recorded
Never performed 

© December 16, 2019

excerpt.rendered: Abandoned almost as soon as Bruce began it, “In Kansas” provides a glimpse of what might have developed into an early epic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 17
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce films the video for "Tunnel of Love," releases his first album collection, plays the second of two amazing Christic shows, and serenades Taylor Swift--all this and much more inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: It’s All Over Now
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Rolling Stones' first #1 U.K. hit had a habit of turning up in Bruce's set lists in the strangest places, but fortunately a couple of his team-ups were captured for posterity.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cover Me, Brandi Carlile: Born to Run
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the wake of North Carolina's anti-LGBTQ HB2 law, Bruce made a statement by cancelling his show in Greensboro. Brandi Carlile made a different kind of statement shortly after–and it was perfect.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Ricky Wants a Man of Her Own
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Ricky Wants a Man of Her Own" is a fun, poppy outtake from the River sessions--guaranteed to make you smile (unless you're a parent to a teenage girl, in which case you'll wince).

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 7
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce plays his second album start-to-finish for the first time, debuts a new arrangement for "Blinded by the Light," and plays a last-ditch rally for Hillary Clinton on Election Eve.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Something You Got
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Bruce and Dr. John performed together for the first time, they reached way back in both of their set lists to find the perfect song.
